newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire's Mobutu vows to end rebel occupation.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu vows to end rebel occupation.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has listed ending rebel occupation of eastern Zaire and preparing the chaotic country for pluralist elections as his main priorities for 1997, Kenya's presidential press agency said on Tuesday.
The agency was reporting on a one-day summit in Zaire on Monday between Mobutu and Kenya's Daniel arap Moi called to discuss Africa's latest civil war.
Zairean rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) have captured a large part of eastern Zaire since war broke out last October.
The rebels led by longtime Mobutu opponent, Laurent Kabila, have vowed to march to Kinshasa to overthrow Mobutu who has ruled the mineral-rich country for 31 years.

"The Zairean delegation said priorities of the government of Zaire this year are to put finishing touches to the democratisation process in respect to the electoral agenda," the agency said in a report released on Tuesday.
It added: "Another priority is to sustain efforts in order to put an end to the occupation of a portion of Zairean territory by rebels."
Regional analysts said efforts to hold elections in Zaire will be hampered by a lack of infrastructure in the vast central African nation and because of the war.
Moi flew to Mobutu's jungle palace at Gbadolite following a summit, boycotted by Kinshasa, of 10 African leaders in Nairobi last December which discussed eastern Zaire.

The agency said a communique issued after Monday's talks reaffirmed the presidents' commitment to territorial integrity and the inviolability of boundaries in accordance with the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) and U.N. charters.

"They also reaffirmed the fact that the principles of national sovereignty, territorial integrity, inviolability of boundaries and the issues concerning citizenship are not negotiable," the agency said.
Moi and the presidents of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Cameroon were entrusted by the Nairobi summit to secure an early meeting with Mobutu to discuss ways of resolving the central African crisis.
The Alliance rebels have seized a swath of eastern Zaire from the army including Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
Over Christmas they took the strategic gold mining centre of Bunia in Upper Zaire province near the Ugandan border.
The Zairean government has vowed to recover all the territory from the rebels and forces from neighbouring states it accuses of backing them.

Kenya and Zaire deplored the "indecisiveness of the international community" in implementing a U.N. resolution for deployment of multinational troops for humanitarian reasons in eastern Zaire, the agency said.
Africa's latest war in Zaire was sparked off by Zairean attempts to expel back to Rwanda the Banyamulenge -- an ethnic Tutsi group which migrated to Zaire up to 200 years ago.

The government has ruled out negotiation with Kabila but analysts say Zaire is not in a position to inflict heavy losses on the better equipped rebels. Many politicians are increasingly in favour of a peaceful settlement.
